stations.title: Doorbell

peripheral.name: Doorbell button
peripheral.blurb: Dry contact (wet/NPN/PNP also OK, 5–36 V) — optocoupled, never touches the S3.

stations.instructions:
Wire (supply OFF first):
1. External 5-24 V DC supply "+" -> DI COM.
2. Doorbell button between supply "-" and DI0
   (dry contact; wet/NPN/PNP also OK, 5-36 V).
3. Power the supply, press the button.
Presses count here and pulse DO0 (the "ding" link).
Safe: DI is optocoupled - it never touches the S3.

stations.title: Intrusion

peripheral.name: PIR / reed / beam-break
peripheral.blurb: PIR, reed contact, or laser break-beam receiver — relay or open-collector output.

stations.instructions:
PIR / reed contact / laser break-beam receiver:
1. Supply "+" -> DI COM (shared with DI0).
2. Sensor output (relay or open-collector) between
   supply "-" and DI1.
3. For a beam-gap sensor: aim emitter at receiver;
   breaking the beam trips DI1 - the held-ms readout
   is your gap timing.

stations.title: Chime out

peripheral.name: Chime / buzzer
peripheral.blurb: Chime, LED, or relay coil (add a flyback diode across coils). Driven, never sensed.

stations.instructions:
Isolated open-drain output (max 450 mA sink):
1. External supply "+" -> load "+" (chime, LED,
   relay coil - add a flyback diode across coils).
2. Load "-" -> DO0. Supply "-" -> the isolated GND.
3. PULSE drives 1.5 s; LATCH holds 30 s max.
Every drive is bounded - outputs release themselves.

stations.title: Strobe out

peripheral.name: Strobe / siren
peripheral.blurb: Second isolated output — a strobe/siren candidate while DO0 holds the chime.

stations.instructions:
Second isolated output - same wiring as DO0.
Use it for a strobe/siren candidate while DO0
holds the chime, to test both alert voices at
once. PULSE = 1.5 s, LATCH auto-releases at 30 s.

stations.title: Light

peripheral.name: Ambient light sensor
peripheral.blurb: VEML7700 (0x10, preferred) or BH1750 strapped to 0x5C — its default 0x23 is the CH422G's.

stations.instructions:
Ambient light sensor on the I2C terminal:
1. VEML7700 (addr 0x10, preferred) or BH1750 with
   ADDR strapped HIGH (0x5C - its default 0x23 is
   the CH422G's, do not use it!).
2. VOUT->VCC GND->GND SDA->SDA SCL->SCL.
   Check VOUT is 5 V or 3.3 V per your sensor.
Hot-plug OK - the census attaches it in ~3 s.

stations.title: ToF range

peripheral.name: VL53L0X ToF
peripheral.blurb: Time-of-flight ranging (0x29). Under the TRIP threshold counts one trip — a laser-gap prototype.

stations.instructions:
VL53L0X time-of-flight on the I2C terminal
(addr 0x29). Wire like the light sensor.
Live mm readout; dropping under the TRIP
threshold counts one trip - point it across a
doorway and it is your laser-gap prototype.
Bench driver: uncalibrated, +/- a few percent.

stations.title: Cap touch

peripheral.name: MPR121 pad
peripheral.blurb: 12-electrode controller (0x5A). Cycle sensitivity for the printed shell-thickness coupon test.

stations.instructions:
MPR121 12-pad controller (addr 0x5A).
Shell-thickness test (printed plastic coupons):
1. Tape a coupon over an electrode.
2. Cycle SENSITIVITY until a finger through the
   coupon registers reliably, no ghost touches.
3. Note preset vs thickness in the bench log -
   that pair is the enclosure design input.

stations.title: I2C census
stations.instructions:
Live scan of the shared GPIO8/9 bus (every 3 s).
Reserved here: 0x23/0x24/0x26/0x38 = CH422G
commands, 0x5D/0x14 = GT911. A sensor set to a
reserved address will misbehave AND can glitch
backlight/touch - re-strap it before wiring.
